The '''Al-Khalid/VT-1A''' ({{langx|ur|{{Nastaliq|الخالد ٹینک}}}} — {{Transliteration|ur|''Al-Xālid Ṫaiŋk''}}, {{IPA|hns|əlˈxaːlɪd̪ ʈɛːŋk|pron}}, {{Lit|The Eternal Tank}}) is a [[main battle tank]] family developed jointly by [[Norinco]] of China and [[Heavy Industries Taxila]] of Pakistan. The tank is based on the Type 90-II tank and it's predecessor.<ref name="Dawn">{{cite web|title=Pakistan's tool of war: Al-Khalid Main Battle Tank – the armoured fist|date=10 November 2015|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1217909|author=Ali Osman|access-date=3 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170407003207/https://www.dawn.com/news/1217909|archive-date=7 April 2017|url-status=live|newspaper=Dawn (newspaper)}}</ref> Approximately 300 Al-Khalid main battle tanks were produced by 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.senate.gov.pk/uploads/documents/1428039146_666.pdf |title=Report Of The Standing Committee On Defence Production |access-date=3 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170101231447/http://www.senate.gov.pk/uploads/documents/1428039146_666.pdf |archive-date=1 January 2017 |website=Senate of Pakistan website|url-status=live}}</ref> The tank has been exported by China to Bangladesh, Morocco and Myanmar. The VT-1A is also marketed as the '''MBT-2000'''.

The [[Bangladesh Army]] ordered 44 MBT-2000s from China in 2011.<ref name="thedailystar1">{{cite web |author=Hasan Jahid Tusher |url=http://archive.thedailystar.net/newDesign/news-details.php?nid=191737 |title=Army to get 44 tanks |work=[[The Daily Star (Bangladesh)]] |date=27 June 2011 |access-date=3 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130916084233/http://archive.thedailystar.net/newDesign/news-details.php?nid=191737 |archive-date=16 September 2013 |url-status=live |df=dmy }}</ref><ref name="page44">{{cite web |last=Dunnigan |first=James |title=Chinese Tanks For Everyone |url=http://www.strategypage.com/dls/articles/Chinese-Tanks-For-Everyone-5-6-2012.asp |publisher=strategypage.com |access-date=3 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120508221311/http://www.strategypage.com/dls/articles/Chinese-Tanks-For-Everyone-5-6-2012.asp |archive-date=8 May 2012 |url-status=live |df=dmy }}</ref> The Norinco-made MBT-2000 is also used by the [[Royal Moroccan Army]].<ref name="strategypage1">{{cite web |url=http://www.strategypage.com/htmw/htarm/20100803.aspx |title=Armor: Chinese Tanks In North Africa |url-status=live |access-date=3 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100808022110/http://www.strategypage.com/htmw/htarm/20100803.aspx |archive-date=8 August 2010 |df=dmy }}</ref> It was trialed by the [[Peruvian Army]] for possible acquisition, but was not purchased due to financial problems.<ref name="The trouble tank MBT-2000 Peru: details">{{cite web|title=The trouble tank MBT-2000 Peru: details|url=http://survincity.com/2013/05/the-trouble-tank-mbt-2000-peru-details/|access-date=3 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161009225819/http://survincity.com/2013/05/the-trouble-tank-mbt-2000-peru-details/|archive-date=9 October 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Operated by a crew of three and armed with a 125&nbsp;mm [[Tank gun#Smoothbore|smooth-bore]] [[tank gun]] that is [[autoloader|reloaded automatically]], the tank uses a [[fire-control system]] and night-fighting equipment.<ref name="CiarAK">{{cite news |last=F Foss |first=Christopher |title=Al Khalid MBT to enter production |url=http://www.ciar.org/ttk/mbt/pakistan.al-khalid.100701043433.html |access-date=3 October 2021|date=22 November 2000 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030518213038/http://www.ciar.org/ttk/mbt/pakistan.al-khalid.100701043433.html |archive-date=18 May 2003 |url-status=live |df=dmy }}</ref> Al-Khalid is named after the 7th-century Muslim commander [[Khalid bin al-Walid]] (592–642 AD).<ref name="brecorder">{{cite news |title=Modernisation of Al-Khalid tank: Ukraine to provide technical cooperation to Pakistan: envoy |url=http://www.brecorder.com/general-news/single/599/0:/1243705:modernisation-of-al-khalid-tank-ukraine-to-provide-technical-cooperation-to-pakistan-envoy/?date=2011-10-20 |access-date=3 October 2021 |newspaper=Business Recorder (newspaper)|date=20 October 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402232418/http://www.brecorder.com/general-news/single/599/0:/1243705:modernisation-of-al-khalid-tank-ukraine-to-provide-technical-cooperation-to-pakistan-envoy/?date=2011-10-20 |archive-date=2 April 2015 |url-status=live |df=dmy }}</ref><ref name="Encyclopaedia" />

The current production variant of the Al-Khalid uses a diesel engine and transmission supplied by the [[Kharkiv Morozov Machine Building Design Bureau|KMDB]] design bureau of Ukraine.<ref name="CiarAK" /><ref name="Ukraine">{{cite news |url=http://en.ria.ru/business/20130218/179551243.html |title=Ukraine to Deliver 110 Battle Tank Engines to Pakistan |agency=SPUTNIK International |date=18 February 2013 |access-date=3 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130225043806/http://en.ria.ru/business/20130218/179551243.html |archive-date=25 February 2013 |url-status=live |df=dmy }}</ref> The first production models entered service with the Pakistan Army in 2001. The country placed an order with Ukraine to further upgrade the tanks with a new engine.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.janes.com/article/65742/ukraine-to-provide-engines-for-pakistan-s-improved-al-khalid-mbt |title=Janes {{pipe}} Latest defence and security news |access-date=24 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161125043613/http://www.janes.com/article/65742/ukraine-to-provide-engines-for-pakistan-s-improved-al-khalid-mbt |archive-date=25 November 2016 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==History==
{{Original research|date=June 2021}}
The [[People's Liberation Army|Chinese People's Liberation Army]] was concerned about the [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] threat, required an improved main battle tank (MBT) to replace the old and obsolete [[Type 59 tank]]. Thus, in 1980, [[Norinco]] was formed and the Inner Mongolia First Machine Group Corporation was tasked with developing a series of new tanks.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.norinco.com/ |title=Norinco |publisher=Norinco.com website|access-date=3 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130617012315/http://norinco.com/ |archive-date=17 June 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref>

A joint development deal was signed with Pakistan in January 1990.<ref name="paktribune">{{cite news|url=http://www.paktribune.com/news/print.php?id=183554|title=Al Khalid MBT-2000 / Type 2000 Main Battle Tank|date=9 July 2007|newspaper=PakTribune.com (newspaper)|access-date=3 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131104051608/http://www.paktribune.com/news/print.php?id=183554|archive-date=4 November 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> Initial Chinese-built prototypes were tested in Pakistan in August 1991. Pakistan completed its manufacturing plant at Taxila in 1992. Pakistan spent more than [[US$]]20 million over the next eight years on the co-development of a model suitable for its needs and on creating a capability to manufacture it locally.<ref name="paktribune" /> The Project Director at [[Heavy Industries Taxila|Heavy Industries Taxila (HIT)]] Brigadier Nasir Mahmood SI(M) led Pakistan's first indigenously produced tank from conception to production. His team modified the tank to accept a foreign-built engine. Several different prototypes were evaluated.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://rupeenews.com/2008/02/pakistans-500-al-khalid-tanks-have-beeen-in-production-since-2001-newer-generational-tanks-now-being-exported-via-ideas-2008/ |title=Pakistan's 500 Al-Khalid tanks have been in production since 2001: Newer generational tanks now being exported via IDEAS 2008 |publisher=Rupee News |access-date=3 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130317133453/http://rupeenews.com/2008/02/pakistans-500-al-khalid-tanks-have-beeen-in-production-since-2001-newer-generational-tanks-now-being-exported-via-ideas-2008/ |archive-date=17 March 2013}}</ref>

In light of high ambient temperatures and the fine sand or dust that would be encountered in operational areas such as the deserts of southern Pakistan, the development of high performance cooling and air filtering systems was emphasized during the planning stage of the project. Implementation of a hydro-gas suspension system was considered but, after technical evaluation, it was found to be impractical due to various limitations such as problems with reliability and maintainability. Installation of the [[Renk|Renk 304]] transmission was also considered but discarded.

An early version was armed with a Chinese gun and [[fire-control system]], and had a German-designed [[MTU Friedrichshafen|MTU]]-396 diesel engine which was built under licence in China. Another version was equipped with a more advanced Western digital fire-control system and powered by a Perkins {{convert|1200|hp|abbr=on}} Condor diesel engine (as in the British [[Challenger 1 tank|Challenger]]) and SESM ESM500 [[automatic transmission]] (as in the French [[Leclerc tank|Leclerc]]). This version{{Which|date=June 2021}} was considered too expensive, and under-performed in the extreme heat of southern Pakistan. Finally, a version{{Which|date=June 2021}} was tested with the compact Ukrainian 6TD-2 1,200&nbsp;hp diesel engine.<ref name="Ukraine"/> This configuration was chosen by Pakistan for the production version of the tank and came to be known as Al-Khalid.

The final tank design resulting from a decade of co-operative development was designated ''Type 90-IIM''. The Chinese company Norinco showed the new Type 90-IIM during the March 2001 Abu Dhabi Defense Expo, under the export name ''MBT 2000''. The version powered by the Ukrainian engine, intended for domestic production in Pakistan, was named ''Al-Khalid''.<ref name="military-today2">{{Cite web |author=ARG |url=http://www.military-today.com/tanks/type_90_II.htm |title=Type 90-II - Main battle tank |access-date=23 June 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130118113826/http://www.military-today.com/tanks/type_90_II.htm |archive-date=18 January 2013 |url-status=dead |df=dmy }}</ref>

During the development period, [[Heavy Industries Taxila]] gained experience after building the [[Type 85-IIAP]] under Chinese licence and prepared to begin production of the Al-Khalid tank in 1999. A pilot batch of fifteen tanks was inducted into the 31st Cavalry Regiment of Pakistan's Armoured Corps on 20 July 2001. Pakistan signed a contract with Ukraine's [[Malyshev Factory]] in May 2002 for the delivery of 315 [[Kharkiv Morozov Machine Building Design Bureau|KMDB 6TD-2]] diesel engines over three years.<ref name="pakistandefence">{{cite web |url=http://www.pakistanidefence.com/news/MonthlyNewsArchive/2002/April2002.htm |title=Pakistan's, $150 Million Contract Signed With Ukraine |date=April 2002 |publisher=PakistanDefence.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020421161219/http://www.pakistanidefence.com/news/MonthlyNewsArchive/2002/April2002.htm |archive-date=21 April 2002 |url-status=dead |df=dmy |access-date=11 August 2007 }}</ref> An additional batch of Al-Khalid tanks was delivered on 23 September 2004. Pakistan planned to build a total of 600 Al-Khalid tanks for its [[Pakistan Armed Forces|armed forces]].<ref name="globalsecurity">{{cite web|url=http://www.globalsecurity.org/military/world/pakistan/mbt-2000.htm|title=Al Khalid MBT-2000 / Type 2000 Main Battle Tank|publisher=GlobalSecurity.org | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131104171710/http://www.globalsecurity.org/military/world/pakistan/mbt-2000.htm | archive-date=4 November 2013}}</ref>

In December 2017, HIT officials told the Pakistan Senate that budgetary constraints had reduced the output of the tank to 18 per year on average.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.janes.com/article/76098/fiscal-constraints-hit-pakistan-s-production-of-al-khalid-i-tanks|title=Fiscal constraints hit Pakistan's production of Al-Khalid-I tanks {{!}} Jane's 360|website=www.janes.com|access-date=2017-12-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171206233831/http://www.janes.com/article/76098/fiscal-constraints-hit-pakistan-s-production-of-al-khalid-i-tanks|archive-date=6 December 2017|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

On July 28, 2020, the [[Pakistan Army]] inducted the first Al Khalid-I main battle tank into its Armoured Corps Regiment. The handing over ceremony of the tank, which is an upgraded version of Al Khalid tank, was held at HIT.

==Unveiling==
The Al-Khalid was unveiled on 17 July 1991 by the [[Prime Minister of Pakistan|Prime Minister]] [[Nawaz Sharif]] and [[Chief of Army Staff (Pakistan)|Chief of Army Staff]] [[Mirza Aslam Beg]] during a ceremony at the [[Heavy Industries Taxila|Heavy Rebuild Factory (HRF)]], [[Taxila (modern)|Taxila]]. In his speech, the Prime Minister said that the completion of the project was a big step towards self-reliance. The Army Chief said that for the first time in history, not only had technology been transferred to Pakistan, but the design was also made by Pakistani engineers themselves.<ref name=Encyclopaedia>{{cite book|title=Pakistan Chronicle|year=2010|publisher=Wirsa Publications|location=Karachi|isbn=9789699454004|page=688|author=Aqeel Abbas Jafari|edition=1st|language=ur}}</ref>

==Design==
===Armament===
Al-Khalid is designed with a 125&nbsp;mm bore, 48 calibre long [[smoothbore]], autofrettaged and chrome-plated gun barrel which is manufactured from high strength electroslag remelting steel.{{citation needed|date= June 2021}} The gun is then put under stringent quality control process to ensure standard barrel life of 1,100 rounds [[Glossary_of_British_ordnance_terms#Effective_full_charge|EFC]]; barrels that cannot pass this test are rejected. This gun provides very high internal chamber pressures for APFSDS, HEAT-FS and guided missiles.{{citation needed|date= June 2021}}  The gun can also fire the following types of conventional ammunition: [[APFSDS]], [[HEAT-FS]], and [[HE-FS]]. The gun is a modified variant of both the ZPT-98 and KBA-3 series of 125&nbsp;mm smooth bore gun for Al-Khalid MBT which provided compatibility with Ukrainian ATGMs such as Kombat.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}} The gun retains qualities of both Chinese and Ukrainians mated with indigenous design for better and accurate firepower on stationary and moving targets alike.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}} The Gun-launched, laser-guided [[anti-tank guided missile]]s can also be launched.<ref>{{citation |publisher=Cast |place=RU |url=http://mdb.cast.ru/mdb/2-2001/ff/atdjm/?form=print |title=MDB |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041227174113/http://mdb.cast.ru/mdb/2-2001/ff/atdjm/?form=print |archive-date=27 December 2004 |url-status=live |df=dmy }}</ref><ref name="iasc">{{cite web |url=http://www.strategycenter.net/research/pubID.48/pub_detail.asp |title=Report On the International Defense Exhibition and Seminar (IDEAS) |date=29 October 2004 |author=Richard Fisher Jr |publisher=International Assessment and Strategy Center |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050709081957/http://www.strategycenter.net/research/pubID.48/pub_detail.asp |archive-date=9 July 2005 |url-status=dead |df=dmy }}</ref>{{Failed verification|date=June 2021|reason=none of the cited sources says AL Khalid can fire laun launched laser guided anti tank guided missile}}

Al-Khalid also fires a Pakistani [[depleted uranium]] round{{citation needed|date=June 2021}}, the Naiza 125&nbsp;mm DU round which gives an armour penetration of 570&nbsp;mm RHA at 2&nbsp;km.<ref>{{citation |url=http://www.acig.org/artman/publish/article_4.shtml |title=IDEAS 2002 Defence Expo Report |publisher=ACIG |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030408131704/http://www.acig.org/artman/publish/article_4.shtml |archive-date=8 April 2003 |url-status=usurped |df=dmy }}</ref>{{irrelevant citation|date=June 2021|reason=Cited source doen not says Al khalid can fire depleted Uranium round, its name, depth of penetration}}{{citation needed|date=June 2021}} It is equipped with a muzzle reference system and dual-axis stabilisation system.<ref name = "HITMBT" /> Elevation and azimuth control is achieved by electro-hydraulic power drives. The automatic ammunition-handling system for the main gun has a 24-round ready-to-fire magazine and can load and fire at a rate of eight rounds per minute.<ref name="HITMBT">{{citation |url=http://www.depo.org.pk/index.php?id=7&a=org_prod_listings&pid=43&product=Armoured%20Fighting%20Vehicles%20and%20Upgrades | publisher = Depo | place = PK | title = Heavy Industries Taxila | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120219193339/http://www.depo.org.pk/index.php?id=7&a=org_prod_listings&pid=43&product=Armoured%20Fighting%20Vehicles%20and%20Upgrades | archive-date=19 February 2012}}</ref>

The tank is also equipped with a 7.62&nbsp;mm-coaxial machine gun, a 12.7&nbsp;mm remotely {{Citation needed|date=July 2021}}controlled externally mounted air-defence machine gun that can be aimed and fired from within the tank, and 16 smoke grenade launchers(12 Smoke, 4HE).

The gunner is provided with a dual-magnification day sight and the commander with a panoramic sight for all-around independent surveillance.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}} Both sights are dual-axis image stabilised and have independent laser range-finders. The tank has hunter-killer capability, giving the commander the ability to acquire new targets independently while the gunner is engaging another target.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}} The automatic target-tracking system is designed to work when tank and target are both moving.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}} [[Night vision]] for the gunner and commander is achieved through a dual-magnification [[Thermography|thermal imaging]] sight. Both sights are integrated with the fire-control system.<ref name="HITMBT" />  The production Al-Khalid tank's fire-control system is the ISFCS-122B and is a modified version of the Chinese ISFCS-122 modified with French Assistance by adding features like Auto-tracking and more. In the MBT 2000, the Chinese Norinco fire-control system takes inputs from ten sensors.  The ballistic computation time is less than one second. The manufacturer claims routine first round hits on standard {{convert |8|ft|m|abbr=on}} square targets at ranges over 2,000 metres.

* Effective range: 200 to 7,000 metres{{clarify|reason=effective range of what?|date=June 2021}}
* Sensor: laser ranging from 200 to 9,990 metres
* French Auto-tracking, interfaced with gunner station, firing four types of munitions, gunner's thermal imaging sight, commander's image intensification night vision sight, gyro-stabilised and UPS power supply system.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}}

Prototypes were demonstrated with various fire-control systems of Chinese and western origin, but the production model of the Al-Khalid MBT's use a modified Chinese fire-control system (FCS) and gun control system (GCS).

The Al-Khalid-1's FCS has been improved and is able to cue up multiple targets at once and has Auto-tracking for both the 125mm Main gun as well as for the 12.7mm Anti-air gun.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}} It is also equipped with the "Integrated Battlefield Management System" (IBMS), named "Rebar", a digital communications system developed domestically by HIT and CARE (Centre for Advanced Research in Engineering). It comprises a flat-screen display mounted inside the tank which communicates with those of other vehicles, including command posts such as the [[Sakb|HIT Sakb]]. It uses a [[data-link]] to facilitate secure communication of battlefield information between units, including tank video footage and information from [[unmanned aerial vehicle]]s.<ref name="iasc" />

A project to manufacture the first Pakistani tank gun barrel was started by Pakistan's Strategic Plans Division (SPD) in 2000. In April 2011, it was reported that the first Pakistani-produced tank gun barrel was ready to be delivered to HIT for installation on the Al-Khalid and [[Al-Zarrar]].<ref name="autogenerated2">{{cite web |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/621771/locally-produced-gun-delivered-to-hit-for-tanks |title=Locally-produced gun delivered to HIT for tanks {{pipe}} |newspaper=Dawn (newspaper) |date=18 April 2011 |access-date=3 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150918220008/http://www.dawn.com/news/621771/locally-produced-gun-delivered-to-hit-for-tanks |archive-date=18 September 2015 |url-status=live |df=dmy}}</ref> Previously, HIT imported 125&nbsp;mm gun barrel blanks from France for the two tanks which would then be machined in Pakistan by HIT. The first Pakistani gun barrel blank was produced at Heavy Mechanical Complex (HMC) in a joint project involving HIT, People's Steel Mills Limited (PSML) and other defence-related organisations.<ref name="autogenerated2"/> The specialist grade steel was produced at PSML and the resulting steel block was passed on to HMC. HMC then pressed the block to a length of 5 metres and square cross-section, before forging it into a 125&nbsp;mm smoothbore barrel. The barrel was then heat treated several times in facilities such as a large vertical furnace. The process took 2–3 months and was watched by experts from other defence-related organisations. The barrel was to be capable of firing at 4 rounds per minute as well as being compatible with the autoloader and its 24-round magazine.<ref name="autogenerated2"/> According to a HIT official, a joint team proved to the [[Pakistan Army]] that strict standards would be met before the army approved production of a first batch of 50 gun barrels by HMC. The Pakistani gun barrels would likely be installed on upgraded versions of the Al-Khalid which are under development by HIT. A 200 million PKR contract has been finalised by HIT for the first 50 barrel batch, which is slightly lower than the barrels imported from France. After production of the first batch of local tank gun barrels in 2011, Heavy Mechanical Complex is planning to explore manufacture of artillery guns.<ref name="autogenerated2"/><ref>{{cite web |publisher=Daiji World |url=http://www.daijiworld.com/news/news_disp.asp?n_id=99597&n_tit=Pakistan+Produces+its+First+Tank+Gun |title=Pakistan Produces its First Tank Gun |access-date=3 May 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121013084730/http://www.daijiworld.com/news/news_disp.asp?n_id=99597&n_tit=Pakistan+Produces+its+First+Tank+Gun |archive-date=13 October 2012 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

===Mobility===
The production model Al-Khalid is powered by a 6TD-2 liquid-cooled [[diesel engine]], designed by the [[Kharkiv Morozov Machine Building Design Bureau|Kharkiv Morozov Design Bureau (KMDB)]] of [[Ukraine]]. The 6TD-2 is a [[supercharged]] 6-cylinder engine delivering {{convert|1,200|hp|kW}}.<ref name="morozov1">{{cite web |url=http://www.morozov.com.ua/eng/body/addmotor.php |title=KMDB – Tank Power Pack with 6TD-2 Engine |publisher=Morozov.com.ua |access-date=20 June 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070618234316/http://www.morozov.com.ua/eng/body/addmotor.php |archive-date=18 June 2007 |url-status=dead |df=dmy }}</ref> The [[2-stroke]] design, with the pistons arranged horizontally in an [[opposed piston engine|opposed piston configuration]], makes the engine very compact and therefore more suitable for being fitted into relatively small vehicles such as the Al-Khalid MBT.<ref name="morozov1"/>

The 6TD-2 is part of a Ukrainian power pack and is capable of semi-automatic power-shifting, the transmission has 7 forward and 4 reverse speeds along with a braking system that incorporates carbon friction brakes and a secondary speed-retarding system. Gear changes are controlled by a [[torque converter]] which is made more efficient by addition of an automatic lock-up clutch. There is also a mechanical back-up system for use in emergencies, able to shift 2 gears forward and reverse.<ref name="morozov1"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://en.uos.ua/produktsiya/bronetehnika/60-tankovie-dizelnie-dvigateli |title=The tank diesel engine |publisher=En.uos.ua (Ukraine website)|access-date=3 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130223075805/http://en.uos.ua/produktsiya/bronetehnika/60-tankovie-dizelnie-dvigateli |archive-date=23 February 2013 |url-status=live |df=dmy }}</ref>

The Al-Khalid is fairly lightweight compared to the Western tanks, weighing 46 tonnes compared to the 60 tonne [[M1 Abrams]] and [[Leopard 2]].<ref name="dj2">{{cite web |url= http://www.defencejournal.com/2001/august/armaments.htm |title=Towards Self-reliance in Armaments |date=August 2001 | first =Sardar F.S. | last = Lodi | work =Defence Journal |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20011108095913/http://defencejournal.com/2001/august/armaments.htm |archive-date=8 November 2001 |url-status=dead |df= dmy}}</ref> A [[power-to-weight ratio]] of 26.66 [[hp/tonne]] gives acceleration from 0 to 32&nbsp;km/h (0 to 20&nbsp;mph) in 10 seconds and a maximum speed of 72&nbsp;km/h, the speed and agility also helping to improve survivability.<ref name="dj2"/>

A [[Vehicle snorkel|snorkel]] allows the tank to cross water obstacles up to 5 metres deep, after some preparation by the crew. Navigation is assisted by an [[inertial navigation system|inertial navigation system (INS)]] and a [[GPS]] satellite navigation system.{{Citation needed |date=October 2017}}

===Protection===
Al-Khalid has modular composite armour and [[explosive reactive armour]], high hardened steel plates over rolled homogeneous layers. The composite armour includes classified elements and NERA inserts.{{citation needed|date= June 2021}}  The vehicle also has overpressure nuclear-biological-chemical defense system, an effective thermal smoke generator, internal fire extinguisher and explosion-suppression system.  The infrared signature of the tank is reduced by infrared reflective paint.{{citation needed |date=June 2021}} The Al-Khalid's armour is publicly stated to be around 660mm vs HEAT and 550mm vs APFSDS without ERA on the Turret and the Glacis is Estimated to be around 450-470mm without ERA.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}} The Al-Khalid-1 later inducted into the Pakistan Army is improved further from the Al-Khalid 1 unveiled earlier and is equipped with newly developed indigenous explosive reactive armor AORAK Mk.2, which is not only lightweight, but also more resistant to APFSDS, HEAT and HE-FS rounds. ERA is developed by [[Global Industrial Defence Solutions]] (GIDS).<ref name="janes"/> Al-Khalid is also equipped with an active protection system known as VARTA.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}} HIT is working on an indigenous APS system for future batches, especially for Al-Khalid 2.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}}

An advanced laser detection system from ATCOP has been added. The LTS&nbsp;1 consists of a mast-mounted sensor and operator's control box, which includes a display showing threats 360 degrees around the tank.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}} It can detect [[laser rangefinder]]s and [[laser target designator]]s and responds automatically by triggering acoustic alarms, smoke generators and other countermeasure systems. LTS&nbsp;1 can detect laser devices operating in the 0.8 to 1.06&nbsp;μm waveband, has a 360° field of view in azimuth (resolution of 15°) and a field of view in elevation of -15° to +90°.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}}

The Laser Threat Sensor LTS786P is an early warning device which gives audio and visual alarms of threat by sensing a laser beam aimed at it from any direction.<ref>{{Cite web |title=GIDS - Products |url=https://www.gids.com.pk/land#laser |access-date=2025-02-18 |website=www.gids.com.pk}}</ref> The exact location of the threat (incoming beam) is indicated by nine LEDs, covering all directions above the horizon. It has the capability to differentiate between a Laser Range Finder, Laser Target Designator or a Laser Target Tracker Signal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Product Search |url=https://depo.gov.pk/single_product.php?pid=140 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220726185050/https://depo.gov.pk/single_product.php?pid=140 |archive-date=26 Jul 2022 |website=Defense export promotion organisation}}</ref> Provision of sensor output signal, interfacing for appropriate countermeasures, is also available. It can be used on stationary or moving objects of any size or shape. The maximum operating range is 10&nbsp;km.<ref name="GIDS195">{{cite web |url=http://www.gids.com.pk/ta_Backup/prodetail.php?prodid=195 |title= Laser Threat Sensor (LTS786P) |publisher=Gids |access-date=21 September 2011 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160113183129/http://www.gids.com.pk/ta_Backup/prodetail.php?prodid=195 |archive-date=13 January 2016 |url-status=live |df= dmy}}</ref>{{irrelevant citation |date=June 2021|reason= source is empty}}{{citation needed |date=June 2021}}

====ATCOP LTS786P specifications====
*Response: enhanced for Nd:YAG laser signal
*Range: >10,000 m
*Field of view: capable of detecting any signal aimed towards LTS786P.
*Detector type: silicon photodiode
*Size (approx.): 214 x 134&nbsp;mm (sensor head)
*126 x 123 x 100&nbsp;mm (display unit)
*Weight 2&nbsp;kg (sensor head), approx.): 1&nbsp;kg (display unit)<ref name="GIDS195"/>

==Variants==
===Prototypes===
* '''Type 90-II'''&nbsp;– A further development of the Type 80/85 series main battle tanks introduced in 1992.<ref name= "military-today2"/>
* '''P1'''&nbsp;– Prototype incorporating a Chinese 125&nbsp;mm gun, autoloader and fire-control system, German MTU-396 diesel engine and Renk LSG-3000 automatic transmission.
* '''P2'''&nbsp;– Prototype incorporating a Chinese 125&nbsp;mm gun and autoloader, Western fire-control system, Perkins 1200&nbsp;hp Condor diesel engine and French SESM ESM500 automatic transmission.
* '''P3'''&nbsp;– Prototype fitted with Chinese 125&nbsp;mm gun and autoloader, Western fire-control system, Ukrainian [[Kharkiv Morozov Machine Building Design Bureau|KMDB]] 6TD-2 1200&nbsp;hp diesel engine and French SESM ESM500 automatic transmission.
* '''P4'''&nbsp;– Prototype export variant incorporating German NATO standard 120&nbsp;mm gun, Western fire-control system, German MTU-871/TCM AVDS-1790 diesel engine and Renk LSG-3000 automatic transmission.

===Production variants===
====Pakistani variants====
[[File:Al-Khalid IDEAS 2012.jpg|thumb|Al-Khalid tank on display at [[International Defence Exhibition and Seminar#Buildup to IDEAS 2012|IDEAS 2012]] held at Expo Center, Karachi, Pakistan in November, 2012.]]

* '''Al-Khalid''' – Based on P3 prototype of MBT-2000, operational as of 2001. Has an ammunition capacity of 39 125&nbsp;mm rounds (22 in autoloader), 500 12.7&nbsp;mm rounds and 3,000 7.62&nbsp;mm rounds.
* '''Al-Khalid I''' – Upgraded variant with ammunition capacity increased to 49 125&nbsp;mm rounds, 1,500 12.7&nbsp;mm rounds and 7,100 7.62&nbsp;mm rounds.<ref name="janes" /><ref name="thenation" /> Incorporates modifications made to the fire-control system which is now a more advanced multi process fire control computer with up to 7&nbsp;km effective identification range. The engagement range is also improved which is up to 3.5&nbsp;km, digital driver panel, IBMS, side-skirts, track pads, digitally controlled FPGA based solid state auto-loader with bidirectional tray movement and ammo availability info on screen, info on empty and full trays and types of available rounds, bigger carousel for longer rounds,<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.hit.gov.pk/ |title= Heavy Industries Taxila|access-date= 23 August 2015|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20151015035008/http://www.hit.gov.pk/ |archive-date= 15 October 2015 |url-status= live}}</ref> (rate of fire increased to 9 rounds per minute), Ukrainian Varta electro-optical jammer (disrupts laser rangefinders, laser designators and anti-tank guided missile tracking systems), [[Sagem]] third-generation thermal imagers for both gunner and Commander and improved air conditioning system.<ref name="Pakpushes">{{cite news|last= Ansari |first=Usman|title= Pakistan Pushes Armor Upgrades| work = [[Defense News]] |date=20 April 2009|url= http://www.defensenews.com/story.php?i=4046009|access-date=29 August 2009|archive-url= https://www.webcitation.org/664yYkjVx?url=http://www.defensenews.com/story.php?i=4046009 |archive-date=11 March 2012 |url-status=dead|df= dmy-all}}</ref> It is the most heavily weaponized tank by tonnage. It is fitted with a 1,200&nbsp;hp Ukrainian engine. Al-Khalid I's top speed is 72&nbsp;km/h, and it weighs 46 tonnes.<ref name="thenation" /><ref name="Pakpushes" />

====Chinese variants====
[[File:Chinese 90-IIM MBT.JPG|thumbnail|right|Chinese 90-IIM]]

* '''Type 90-IIM/MBT-2000'''&nbsp;– Type 90-IIM was introduced in 2000 with Ukraine's KMDB 1,200&nbsp;hp 6TD-2 diesel engine. Export version MBT-2000 introduced in 2001 at a defence exhibition in Abu Dhabi.<ref name= "military-today2" />
* '''VT-1A'''&nbsp;– A new export variant of the Type 90-IIM, with Chinese interior, turret, gun, electronics and armour. It has a Chinese 1300 horsepower engine.<ref>{{cite web |url = http://www.china-defense-mashup.com/vt1a-main-battle-tank-a-twin-young-brother-of-al-khalid-mbt.html |title = VT1A |publisher = China defense mashup |access-date = 14 September 2009 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110120182815/http://www.china-defense-mashup.com/vt1a-main-battle-tank-a-twin-young-brother-of-al-khalid-mbt.html |archive-date = 20 January 2011 |url-status = dead |df = dmy}}</ref>

===Cancelled projects===
* '''Type 90-IIA'''&nbsp;– An export model offered to Pakistan. It was powered by French V-series diesel engine, developing 1 500&nbsp;hp.  Cancelled after France joined the international arms embargo on Pakistan after the [[List of nuclear weapons tests of Pakistan|Pakistan's 1998 nuclear tests]].<ref name= "military-today2"/>

Further production was reputedly on hold due to lack of tank engines, with Ukraine first refusing to provide engines,<ref name= "China has put the tanks MBT-2000 in Morocco and Myanmar">{{cite web|title=China has put the tanks MBT-2000 in Morocco and Myanmar | date = April 2011 | work = Surv. in city |url= http://survincity.com/2011/04/china-has-put-the-tanks-mbt-2000-in-morocco-and.html/}}{{dead link |date = October 2016 |bot= InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted= yes}}</ref> but later promising to deliver 110 new tank engines.<ref name= "Ukraine to Deliver Advanced Tank Engines to Pakistan">{{cite web|title= Ukraine to Deliver Advanced Tank Engines to Pakistan |url= http://www.asian-defence.net/2013/02/ukraine-to-deliver-advanced-tank-engines-to-pakistan.html |access-date=3 October 2021|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160311205809/http://www.asian-defence.net/2013/02/ukraine-to-deliver-advanced-tank-engines-to-pakistan.html|website=Asian Defence News |archive-date=11 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>  Since the 2014 Russian invasion, Ukraine was facing issues in making deliveries of equipment.<ref>{{cite web |title= Ukraine Crisis May Affect Pakistani Defense Contracts|url= https://thediplomat.com/2014/05/ukraine-crisis-may-affect-pakistani-defense-contracts/ |access-date=15 February 2016 | date = April 2014 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160201101558/https://thediplomat.com/2014/05/ukraine-crisis-may-affect-pakistani-defense-contracts/ | work = The diplomat |archive-date= 1 February 2016|url-status=live}}</ref>

* {{flag|Myanmar}} – 180+ VT-1As in service. Received between 2009 and 2013<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://armstrade.sipri.org/armstrade/page/trade_register.php|title=SIPRI Arms Transfers Database|website=Stockholm International Peace Research Institute|access-date=September 7, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100414022558/http://armstrade.sipri.org/armstrade/page/trade_register.php|archive-date=14 April 2010|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Failed contracts===
* {{flag|Malaysia}} – In April 2002, it was reported that Malaysia was considering purchasing the Al-Khalid after evaluation by Malaysian military personnel, but Malaysia eventually backed out without stating any reasons.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://ciar.org/ttk/mbt/mbt/mbt.pakistan.al-khalid.malaysia-purchase.2002-05-15.html |title=Malaysia May Purchase Pakistani Tanks "Al-Khalid", in Construction of Which Ukraine Participates |publisher=Ciar.org |access-date=21 September 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030513153521/http://www.ciar.org/ttk/mbt/mbt/mbt.pakistan.al-khalid.malaysia-purchase.2002-05-15.html |archive-date=13 May 2003 |url-status=live |df=dmy }}</ref>
* {{flag|Peru}} – The Peruvian government had expressed interest in purchasing 80–120 units to complement the fleet of Soviet [[T-55]] tanks in service with the [[Peruvian Army]].<ref name="ap">{{cite news|url=https://news.yahoo.com/s/ap/20091209/ap_on_re_la_am_ca/lt_peru_china_military|title= Peru army plans arms purchase, tests Chinese tanks|date=9 December 2009|agency=Associated Press|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091214032908/http://news.yahoo.com/s/ap/20091209/ap_on_re_la_am_ca/lt_peru_china_military|archive-date=14 December 2009}}</ref> However the deal fell through partly due to the unauthorised export of the Ukrainian engine.<ref>{{Cite web|title = No hay dinero para devolver tanques chinos MBT-2000|url = http://larepublica.pe/01-07-2011/no-hay-dinero-para-devolver-tanques-chinos-mbt-2000|website = larepublica.pe|date = 2011-07-01|access-date = 2015-11-11|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151125192451/http://larepublica.pe/01-07-2011/no-hay-dinero-para-devolver-tanques-chinos-mbt-2000|archive-date = 25 November 2015|url-status = dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_WynITqgKLo|title = ShaChang 20150110 走出国门的"战地之王"|access-date = 12 November 2015|website = Youtube|publisher = HangZhou TV|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160113183128/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_WynITqgKLo|archive-date = 13 January 2016|url-status = live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title = China steals $114 million U.S. defense deal with Peru|url = http://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2012/may/30/china-steals-114-million-us-defense-deal-with-peru/?page=all|website = The Washington Times|access-date = 2015-11-11|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151125190824/http://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2012/may/30/china-steals-114-million-us-defense-deal-with-peru/?page=all|archive-date = 25 November 2015|url-status = live}}</ref>
* {{flag|Saudi Arabia}} – The [[Saudi Arabian Army]] began conducting trials of the Al-Khalid's desert performance in April 2006, after expressing interest in purchasing a batch of the tanks 2 years earlier. No order for the tank was placed later.<ref name="janes"/><ref name="idex">{{cite web|url=http://www.idexnews.com/News.asp/id/810|title=Pakistani tank for Saudi Arabia|publisher=IdexNews.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090816082146/http://www.idexnews.com/News.asp/id/810|archive-date=16 August 2009}}</ref>
* {{flag|Sri Lanka}} – In May 2008, Lt. Gen [[Sarath Fonseka]] of the [[Sri Lanka Army]] held talks with his Pakistan Army counterparts regarding the sale of military equipment, weapons and ammunition. The supply of 22 [[Al-Khalid]] [[main battle tank|MBTs]] to the Sri Lanka Army was reportedly finalised during these talks in a deal worth over US$100 million.<ref name="indianexpress1">{{cite news |url=http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/pak-played-key-role-in-lankas-victory-over-tamil-tigers/467482/ |title=Pak played key role in Lanka's victory over Tamil Tigers |newspaper=The Indian Express (newspaper)|date=28 May 2009 |access-date=3 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140618193018/http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/pak-played-key-role-in-lankas-victory-over-tamil-tigers/467482 |archive-date=18 June 2014 |url-status=live |df=dmy }}</ref> The order was later cancelled by Sri Lanka's Defence Secretary.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://tanknutdave.com/the-al-khalid-main-battle-tank/ |title=The Al-Khalid Main Battle Tank |access-date=15 October 2022}}</ref>
